root_cause.text: The `cpcap-battery` driver requests interrupts using devres (`devm_`) before registering the `power_supply` device, which causes the `power_supply` handle to be freed before the interrupt handler is unregistered during driver removal due to the reverse-order deallocation of devres resources.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows `cpcap_battery_init_interrupts(pdev, ddata)` being moved from before `devm_power_supply_register` to after it in `cpcap_battery_probe()`. The commit message explains that "Using the `devm_` variant for requesting IRQ _before_ the `devm_` variant for allocating/registering the `power_supply` handle, means that the `power_supply` handle will be deallocated/unregistered _before_ the interrupt handler".

bic_trace_step.reason: In `cpcap_battery_probe`, the driver calls `cpcap_battery_init_interrupts` (which requests interrupts using `devm_request_threaded_irq` in `cpcap_battery_init_irq`) on line 748, before registering the power supply device using `devm_power_supply_register` on line 766. Because devres resources are released in the reverse order of their allocation during driver removal, the power supply device will be unregistered and freed before the interrupts are disabled. If an interrupt occurs in this window, `cpcap_battery_irq_thread` will call `power_supply_changed(ddata->psy)` (line 599) using the already freed `ddata->psy` handle, leading to a use-after-free vulnerability.
